# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 12 (Bu-Vb Ss12)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 12 (*Dubbaca*, "Being difficult to correct") is the twelfth rule in the *Saṅghādisesa* section of the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a monk who refuses admonition regarding monastic transgressions and proves obstinate is subject to formal suspension [SuttaCentral]. Its origin story features the monk Channa, who was notoriously proud and intractable when corrected by his fellow monastics [SuttaCentral]. Modern English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the corresponding rule in the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Ss 12) and *Parivāra*, as well as versions across the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya Vinaya lineages preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. A corresponding nun's rule is preserved as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 16 and in non-Theravāda Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅgas [SuttaCentral].

DharmaNexus detects extensive Pali-internal text reuse with other disciplinary procedures, notably *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa* 10, 11, and 13, *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya* 68, the *Kammakkhandhaka* (Cullavagga 11), several Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules, and Vinaya treatises such as the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments link the text to Tibetan canonical and paracanonical Vinaya texts, including the Tibetan *Prātimokṣasūtra* (D0002), *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2), *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104), and *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2), as well as the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu*, agreeing with SuttaCentral on the presence of parallels in the Mūlasarvāstivāda tradition [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
